 CORAM:
 HON'BLE JUSTICE SANGITA DHINGRA SEHGAL (PRESIDENT)
 HON'BLE MS. PINKI, MEMBER (JUDICIAL)

 Present: Mr. Anil Goel and Mr. Aditya Goel, Counsel for the
 complainants.
 Mr. Vaibhav Agnihotri, Mr. Harshit Kiran & Mr. Vidit
 Pratap Singh, counsel for the opposite party.

 PER : HON'BLE MS. PINKI, MEMBER (JUDICIAL)

 JUDGMENT
1. The present complaint has been filed by the Complainants against

 the TDI Infrastructure Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the 'Opposite

 Party') alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. The

 Complainant has prayed for the following reliefs:
a. To refund Rs.48,27,739/- to the complainant with
 interest @ 24% p.a. from the date of complaint till
 the actual realization;
b. To pay a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- to the complainants
 as compensation for causing undue mental and
 physical pain, agony and harassment to the
 complainants;
c. To pay Rs.55,000/- to the complainants on account
 of the cost of the present complaint."
2. The brief facts of the case are that the Opposite Party launched a

 residential township project known as TDI City, Kundli, Sonipat

 (Haryana) and widely publicised the project through

 advertisements, representing that all necessary statutory

 ALLOWED PAGE 2 OF 18
 CC-111/2020 DOD.: 06.07.2026
SURINDER PAL GANDHI & ANR. VS. TDI INFRASTRUCTURE LTD.
approvals had been obtained, there would be no hidden charges,

 and possession of the plot would be delivered within 24 months

 from 26.10.2005. Relying upon the representations and

 assurances made by the Opposite Party, the complainants applied

 for a residential plot measuring 250 sq. yds. and paid a booking

 amount of Rs.4,50,000/- through Cheque Nos. 414801 dated

 26.10.2005 (Rs.1,00,000/-) and 414805 dated 04.11.2005

 (Rs.3,50,000/-). The Opposite Party acknowledged the payments

 by issuing a receipt dated 10.11.2005.
3. Thereafter, the Opposite Party allotted Plot No. J-666, Block-J,

 measuring 250 sq. yds., bearing Customer ID No. KR2-2522, vide

 allotment letter dated 15.01.2006. Subsequently, the area of the

 plot was enhanced to 263.12 sq. yds., whereupon the

 complainants paid the additional amount demanded by the

 Opposite Party.
4. It is the case of the complainants that the Opposite Party raised

 periodical demands towards the sale consideration, which were

 duly complied with by them. The complainants made payments on

 different dates between 03.04.2006 and 07.07.2009, including

 charges towards the enhanced area and EDC/interest. According

 to the complainants, they paid a total sum of Rs.13,27,739/-,

 particulars whereof are as under:

.
Cheque
 Date Amount (Rs.) Particulars
 No.

 04.11.2005 414805 3,50,000 Booking amount
 31.03.2006 414812 1,43,750 Instalment
 03.06.2006 414815 1,23,750 Instalment

 16.09.2006 250102 1,73,125 Instalment
 16.11.2006 250104 1,23,750 Instalment
 15.01.2007 250108 1,23,750 Instalment
 07.07.2009 195369 2,41,489 EDC/Interest and
 other charges
5. The complainants submitted that despite receiving almost the

 entire sale consideration and despite expiry of the promised

 period for delivery of possession, the Opposite Party neither

 completed the development of the project nor handed over

 possession of the allotted plot. It has been alleged that the project

 lacked essential infrastructure and statutory approvals, including

 the occupation/completion certificate, and there was no likelihood

 of completion within a reasonable period.
6. The complainants further alleged that despite repeated requests,

 reminders and personal visits, the Opposite Party failed to refund

 the amount deposited by them. According to the complainants,

 the Opposite Party had also failed to furnish copies of the

 approved layout/site plans and had misrepresented that all

 requisite approvals had already been obtained.
ALLOWED PAGE 4 OF 18
 CC-111/2020 DOD.: 06.07.2026
SURINDER PAL GANDHI & ANR. VS. TDI INFRASTRUCTURE LTD
.
7. It is the grievance of the complainants that the conduct of the

 Opposite Party amounts to deficiency in service and unfair trade

 practice, as the Opposite Party induced them to invest in the

 project on false assurances regarding timely development,

 statutory approvals and delivery of possession, but failed to fulfil

 its contractual obligations.
8. Alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practice on the part

 of the Opposite Party, the complainants have filed the present

 complaint seeking refund of the entire amount deposited by them

 along with interest, compensation for mental agony and

 harassment, and litigation costs.
9. After receiving the complaint notice, Opposite Party submitted its

 written statement.
10. The Opposite Party, in its written statement, has raised

 preliminary objections regarding the maintainability of the

 complaint. It is contended that the present Commission lacked

 pecuniary jurisdiction, the complaint was barred by limitation,

 and the complainants were not 'consumers' within the meaning of

 the
Consumer Protection Act
, as the plot had been purchased for

 investment purposes. It was further alleged that the complainants

 had suppressed material facts, particularly the fact that the

 Opposite Party had, vide letter dated 19.03.2019, offered them the

 option of either accepting an alternative ready-to-possess unit in

 ALLOWED PAGE 5 OF 18
 CC-111/2020 DOD.: 06.07.2026
SURINDER PAL GANDHI & ANR. VS. TDI INFRASTRUCTURE LTD.
the same project or adjusting the deposited amount against

 another project. It is also pleaded that the complainants had

 booked another plot in the same project and had filed a separate

 consumer complaint in respect thereof, thereby demonstrating

 that they were speculative investors.
11. It is further submitted that the complainants had applied for

 allotment of a 250 sq. yd. residential plot, deposited the booking

 amount, and were allotted Plot No. J-667 in the project 'TDI City',

 Sonipat. It also admitted receipt of the amounts paid by the

 complainants from time to time. However, it is denied that the

 complainants had been induced by any false representations or

 that there was any deficiency in service or unfair trade practice on

 its part. According to the Opposite Party, the complainants had

 voluntarily booked the plot after evaluating the project through an

 independent property broker.
12. The Opposite Party denied the allegations regarding delay in

 possession, refusal to refund the deposited amount, lack of

 statutory approvals, and unfair trade practices. It is further

 pleaded that no request for refund or representations had ever

 been made by the complainants and that, in any event, suitable

 alternatives had already been offered to them. The claim for

 refund along with interest @24% per annum, compensation for

 mental agony and litigation expenses was also disputed as being

 ALLOWED PAGE 6 OF 18
 CC-111/2020 DOD.: 06.07.2026
SURINDER PAL GANDHI & ANR. VS. TDI INFRASTRUCTURE LTD.
untenable. On these grounds, the Opposite Party has prayed for

 dismissal of the complaint with costs.
13. The Complainants have filed rejoinder rebutted averments made

 in the written statement filed by the Opposite Party. The

 Complainants have also denied the allegations raised by the

 Opposite Party and reiterated the facts stated in the complaint.
14. The Complainants have filed his evidence by way of affidavit in

 order to prove their averments on record.
15. The Opposite Party has also filed evidence by way of affidavit in

 order to prove its averments on record. An affidavit of Mr. Paras

 Arora S/o Mr. Deepak Arora, Authorized Representative of the

 Opposite Party was filed as evidence of the Opposite Party.
16. Written arguments have been filed on behalf of the Complainant

 and the Opposite Party.
17. We have carefully perused the material available on record as well

 as written submissions filed by either of the parties.
18. The question for consideration before us is whether the present

 complaint is maintainable before this Commission, is not

 barred by limitation, and whether the complainants qualify

 as 'consumers' within the meaning of the
Consumer

 Protection Act
?
ALLOWED PAGE 7 OF 18
 CC-111/2020 DOD.: 06.07.2026
SURINDER PAL GANDHI & ANR. VS. TDI INFRASTRUCTURE LTD
.
19. Before considering the merits of the case, it is necessary to deal

 with the preliminary objections raised by the Opposite Party. The

 Opposite Party has contended that this Commission has no

 pecuniary jurisdiction to entertain the present complaint, that the

 complaint is barred by limitation, and that the complainants are

 not consumers as they had purchased the plot for investment

 purposes.
20. We have considered the submissions of the parties on these

 objections. The first objection relates to the pecuniary jurisdiction

 of this Commission. The Opposite Party has argued that since the

 sale consideration of the plot was only Rs.14,35,000/-, the

 present complaint is not maintainable before this Commission. We

 are unable to accept the said contention. The jurisdiction of the

 Consumer Commission is to be determined in accordance with the

 law applicable on the date of institution of the complaint. Having

 regard to the value of the relief claimed in the present complaint,

 this Commission has the necessary pecuniary jurisdiction to

 entertain and decide the matter. Accordingly, the objection raised

 by the Opposite Party is rejected.
21. The Opposite Party has also pleaded that the complaint is barred

 by limitation since the last payment was made by the

 complainants on 07.07.2009, whereas the present complaint was

 filed much later. We find no merit in this contention. The

 ALLOWED PAGE 8 OF 18
 CC-111/2020 DOD.: 06.07.2026
SURINDER PAL GANDHI & ANR. VS. TDI INFRASTRUCTURE LTD.
grievance of the complainants is that the Opposite Party failed to

 deliver possession of the allotted plot within the promised period

 and also failed to refund the deposited amount. As long as

 possession has not been delivered and the amount has not been

 refunded, the cause of action continues to subsist. It is well

 settled that failure to hand over possession within the stipulated

 or a reasonable period constitutes a continuing cause of action.

 Therefore, the complaint cannot be dismissed on the ground of

 limitation.
22. The Opposite Party has further contended that the complainants

 are speculative investors and, therefore, do not fall within the

 definition of a 'consumer' under the
Consumer Protection Act
.

 This contention is also without substance. The only basis for this

 plea is that the complainants had also booked another plot in the

 same project. However, no documentary evidence has been

 produced by the Opposite Party to establish that the complainants

 were engaged in the business of buying and selling properties or

 that the plots were purchased for any commercial purpose. Mere

 purchase of more than one residential plot is not sufficient to

 conclude that a person is an investor. In the absence of any

 convincing evidence to the contrary, the complainants continue to

 be consumers under the
Consumer Protection Act
and are entitled

 to seek relief under the Act. Accordingly, all the preliminary

 ALLOWED PAGE 9 OF 18
 CC-111/2020 DOD.: 06.07.2026
SURINDER PAL GANDHI & ANR. VS. TDI INFRASTRUCTURE LTD.
objections raised by the Opposite Party regarding pecuniary

 jurisdiction, limitation and the status of the complainants as

 consumers are rejected.
23. The question for consideration before us is whether the Opposite

 Party was guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade

 practice, and if so, whether the complainants are entitled to

 the reliefs claimed?
24. From the perusal of record, it is an admitted fact that the

 complainants booked Plot No. J-667 in the project "TDI City",

 Kundli, Sonipat, and paid a total amount of Rs.15,52,739/- to the

 Opposite Party. The receipt of the said amount and the allotment

 of the plot are not in dispute. The controversy is whether the

 Opposite Party fulfilled its obligation of developing the project and

 handing over possession within the agreed period.
25. According to the complainants, the Opposite Party had assured

 that possession of the allotted plot would be delivered within 24

 months from 26.10.2005 (Advance Registration Form dated

 26.10.2005 annexure R-3 at page No.13 of the written statement).

 However, despite receiving substantial amounts from the

 complainants, the Opposite Party failed to hand over possession

 even after the expiry of the promised period. The complainants

 have stated that the project remained incomplete and lacked basic

 infrastructure and statutory approvals. They, therefore, lost

 ALLOWED PAGE 10 OF 18
 CC-111/2020 DOD.: 06.07.2026
SURINDER PAL GANDHI & ANR. VS. TDI INFRASTRUCTURE LTD.
confidence in the project and sought refund of the amount

 deposited by them.
26. On the other hand, the Opposite Party has denied the allegations

 and submitted that there was no deficiency in service on its part.

 It has relied upon its letter dated 19.03.2019 (Annexure R-2 at

 page No.12 of the written statement), whereby the complainants

 were offered either an alternative ready-to-possess unit in the

 same project or adjustment of the deposited amount in another

 project. According to the Opposite Party, since such alternatives

 were offered, no deficiency in service can be attributed to it.
27. We are unable to accept the above contention. The obligation of

 the Opposite Party was to develop the project and hand over

 possession of the plot originally allotted to the complainants

 within the agreed or a reasonable period. The subsequent offer of

 an alternative unit or adjustment of the deposited amount in

 another project cannot substitute the contractual obligation

 undertaken by the Opposite Party. Rather, such an offer clearly

 indicates that the Opposite Party was not in a position to deliver

 possession of the allotted plot within the stipulated time.
28. The complainants have also specifically pleaded that the project

 was not complete and that the Opposite Party had not obtained

 the necessary statutory approvals. Despite disputing these

 allegations, the Opposite Party has not placed on record any

 ALLOWED PAGE 11 OF 18
 CC-111/2020 DOD.: 06.07.2026
 SURINDER PAL GANDHI & ANR. VS. TDI INFRASTRUCTURE LTD.

 Occupation Certificate, Completion Certificate, or any other

 document to establish that the project had been completed and

 was legally fit for handing over possession. In the absence of such

 material evidence, the plea of the Opposite Party that it was ready

 to deliver possession cannot be accepted.
29. It is a settled principle of law that a builder or developer is under

 both a contractual obligation arising from the terms of the

 Builder-Buyer Agreement and a statutory obligation under the
Consumer Protection Act
to complete the project and deliver

 possession of the allotted unit within the period promised to the

 allottee or, at the very least, within a reasonable time. Where the

 builder fails to honour the committed timeline without any

 justifiable cause, such failure constitutes a clear deficiency in

 service and, in appropriate cases, also amounts to an unfair trade

 practice. The obligation to deliver possession is not merely

 contractual but is coupled with the duty to obtain all requisite

 statutory sanctions, including the Occupancy

 Certificate/Completion Certificate and other approvals necessary

 for lawful occupation of the property. Mere construction of the

 structure without obtaining the mandatory statutory approvals

 does not amount to valid or legal completion of the project.
30. It is equally well settled that a homebuyer cannot be compelled to

 wait indefinitely for possession merely because the builder

 ALLOWED PAGE 12 OF 18
 CC-111/2020 DOD.: 06.07.2026
SURINDER PAL GANDHI & ANR. VS. TDI INFRASTRUCTURE LTD.
continues to hold out assurances of future completion. The

 relationship between the builder and the allottee is founded on

 mutual contractual obligations, and where the builder has

 committed a fundamental breach by failing to complete the project

 within the stipulated or a reasonable period, the allottee acquires

 the right to seek refund of the amounts deposited together with

 appropriate interest and compensation, instead of being forced to

 accept delayed possession. The law recognises that prolonged

 uncertainty defeats the very object for which a residential property

 is purchased, namely, timely shelter and peaceful enjoyment of

 the property.
31. The Hon'ble Supreme Court has consistently held that an allottee

 cannot be expected to wait endlessly where the builder has failed

 to complete the project and obtain the requisite statutory

 approvals.
In
Kolkata West International City Pvt. Ltd. v.

 Devasis Rudra
, (2020) 18 SCC 613, the Supreme Court held that

 failure to deliver possession within the contractual period

 amounts to deficiency in service and that an allottee cannot be

 made to wait indefinitely for possession.
Similarly, in
Pioneer

 Urban Land & Infrastructure Ltd. v. Govindan Raghavan
(2019) 5 SCC 725, the Court observed that where there is an

 unreasonable delay in handing over possession, the purchaser

 cannot be compelled to accept possession at the whim of the

 ALLOWED PAGE 13 OF 18
 CC-111/2020 DOD.
: 06.07.2026
SURINDER PAL GANDHI & ANR. VS. TDI INFRASTRUCTURE LTD.
builder and is entitled to seek refund with appropriate

 compensation.
The same principle was reaffirmed in
IREO Grace

 Realtech Pvt. Ltd. v. Abhishek Khanna
(2021) 3 SCC 241,

 wherein the Supreme Court held that once there is a substantial

 delay in completion of the project, the allottee cannot be forced to

 continue waiting and is entitled to seek refund of the deposited

 amount with interest.
Likewise, in
Experion Developers Pvt. Ltd.

 v. Sushma Ashok Shiroor
(2022) 15 SCC 286, the Supreme

 Court reiterated that delay in handing over possession beyond the

 agreed period constitutes deficiency in service, and an allottee who

 has suffered prolonged delay is entitled to refund with reasonable

 interest rather than being compelled to accept belated possession.
32. Therefore, the settled legal position is that where a builder fails to

 complete the project and deliver lawful possession within the

 promised or a reasonable period, after obtaining all mandatory

 statutory approvals, such failure amounts to deficiency in service

 under the
Consumer Protection Act
. In such circumstances, the

 allottee is legally entitled to refuse delayed possession and claim

 refund of the entire amount deposited along with appropriate

 interest and consequential reliefs.
33. The Hon'ble Supreme Court has repeatedly held that where

 possession is not delivered within the stipulated or a reasonable

 period, the allottee has the option either to accept delayed

 ALLOWED PAGE 14 OF 18
 CC-111/2020 DOD.: 06.07.2026
SURINDER PAL GANDHI & ANR. VS. TDI INFRASTRUCTURE LTD.
possession or to seek refund of the amount deposited with

 reasonable interest. The choice rests with the allottee and not with

 the builder. Once there is an inordinate delay in completion of the

 project, the allottee cannot be compelled to accept possession after

 an uncertain period or to accept an alternative property against

 his wishes.
34. In the present case, the complainants have been waiting for

 possession for several years beyond the promised period. Even

 during the pendency of the present complaint, the Opposite Party

 has failed to establish that the project had been completed or that

 lawful possession could have been offered. The prolonged delay

 has deprived the complainants of the benefit of the property as

 well as the use of the money deposited by them. In such

 circumstances, requiring the complainants to continue waiting for

 possession would be wholly unfair and unjust.
35. We are, therefore, of the considered opinion that the Opposite

 Party has failed to perform its contractual obligations and has

 committed deficiency in service. Its conduct in collecting

 substantial amounts from the complainants without completing

 the project and delivering possession within the promised period

 also amounts to an unfair trade practice. The complainants are,

 therefore, entitled to seek refund of the amount deposited by them

 ALLOWED PAGE 15 OF 18
 CC-111/2020 DOD.: 06.07.2026
SURINDER PAL GANDHI & ANR. VS. TDI INFRASTRUCTURE LTD.
along with appropriate interest and other consequential reliefs in

 accordance with law.
36. Therefore, the complainants have prayed for a refund of

 Rs.48,27,739/-. However, the same is without any basis. In

 paragraphs 6, 7 and 11 of the complaint, the complainants have

 stated that they paid a sum of Rs.13,27,739/-. However, the

 payment details furnished in the table contained in paragraphs 2

 and 4 of the complaint clearly show that the complainants paid

 Rs.15,52,739/-. Further, in its reply to paragraphs 2 and 4 of the

 complaint, the Opposite Party has specifically admitted receipt of

 the said amount of Rs.15,52,739/- from the complainants. An

 admitted fact does not require further proof in view of
Sections 17
to
21
of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, relating to admissions.

 It is well settled that admissions constitute substantive evidence

 against the party making them.
In
Narayan Bhagwantrao

 Gosavi Balajiwale v. Gopal Vinayak Gosavi
, AIR 1960 SC 100,

 the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that an admission is the best

 evidence that the opposite party can rely upon. Though an

 admission is not conclusive, unless it is successfully withdrawn or

 proved to be erroneous, it is decisive of the matter. Therefore, in

 view of
Section 58
of the Indian Evidence Act, facts admitted by

 the parties require no further proof. Accordingly, the admitted

 ALLOWED PAGE 16 OF 18
 CC-111/2020 DOD.
: 06.07.2026
SURINDER PAL GANDHI & ANR. VS. TDI INFRASTRUCTURE LTD.
payment of Rs.15,52,739/- stands established and cannot be

 disregarded while adjudicating the present complaint.
37.
In view of the foregoing discussion and the law
laid down by
the

 Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgments referred to hereinabove,

 we are of the considered opinion that the Opposite Party has failed

 to deliver possession of the allotted plot within a reasonable period

 despite receiving substantial consideration from the complainant

 and, therefore, is clearly guilty of deficiency in service and unfair

 trade practice. Consequently, the present complaint is allowed and

 Opposite Party is directed to refund the entire amount deposited

 by the Complainant towards the plot including all amounts paid

 from time to time i.e., Rs.15,52,739/- along with interest as per

 the following arrangement:
A. An interest @ 6% p.a. calculated from the

 respective dates of deposits till actual realization;

 B. The rate of interest payable as per the aforesaid

 clause (A) is subject to the condition that the

 Opposite Party pays the entire amount on or

 before 05.01.2027;
C. Being guided by the principles as discussed

 above, in case the Opposite Party fails to refund

 the amount as per the aforesaid clause (A) on or

 before 05.01.2027, the entire amount is to be

 ALLOWED PAGE 17 OF 18
 CC-111/2020 DOD.: 06.07.2026
SURINDER PAL GANDHI & ANR. VS. TDI INFRASTRUCTURE LTD
.
refunded along with an interest @ 9% p.a. for the

 period of default till actual realization of the

 amount.
38. In addition to the aforesaid and taking into consideration the

 facts of the present case, the Opposite Party is directed to pay

 a sum of

 A. Rs.50,000/- as cost for mental agony and

 harassment to the complainants; and

 B. The litigation cost to the extent of Rs. 50,000/-.
39. Applications pending, if any, stand disposed of in terms of the

 aforesaid judgment.
40. The judgment be uploaded forthwith on the website of the

 Commission for the perusal of the parties.
41. File be consigned to record room along with a copy of this

 Judgment.
